MANILA, Philippines – After skipping an earlier budget hearing on her office’s proposed budget, Vice President Sara Duterte personally appeared at the Senate on Thursday, November 26, for the plenary deliberations on the Office of the Vice President’s (OVP) proposed P785.24-million budget for 2027.
Senators personally welcomed Duterte before the resumption of the plenary session. The Senate then extended courtesy to the OVP’s proposed budget, approving it after about a minute.

Duterte, who is also facing an impeachment trial before the Senate, declined to answer questions from reporters about the proceedings. Asked for her assessment of the passage of her office’s budget, the Vice President simply replied: “Merry Christmas.”

In October, Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian — who was Senate finance committee chair during the budget deliberations in the previous year — had expressed hope that Duterte would personally defend the OVP’s budget during the plenary deliberations.
The Vice President had skipped an earlier Senate budget hearing to represent her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, in the inurnment of a Davao City official.

The OVP is proposing a P785.2-million budget for next year, with about a third of its proposed operating budget intended for programs on food, transportation, school supplies, livelihood grants, and other forms of aid.

Collectively, the programs put the Office of Vice President Sara Duterte in a highly visible position, delivering aid directly to commuters, students, disaster victims, families, small entrepreneurs, and communities.
That kind of reach carries weight in the context of Philippine politics, where government aid can put politicians in direct contact with voters, especially those seeking higher national office.

Duterte’s planned presidential bid places the programs in a particularly consequential political setting. She faces an ongoing impeachment trial while preparing for a presidential campaign she has already announced for 2028.

If convicted, she will be removed from the vice presidency and disqualified from running for any public office. The impeachment court hopes to finish her trial by the end of 2026. – with reports from Herbie Gomez/ Rappler.com
